sentences.text: The Crime and Misconduct Commission and Griffith University surveyed Queensland custodial officers to track changes in their perceptions of misconduct.
sentences.support: the Crime and Misconduct Commission (CMC) and Griffith University replicated the survey to assess any changes

sentences.text: The research compared officers’ views about misconduct, reporting, training, management and working conditions across surveys in 2001 and 2007.
sentences.support: whether there have been any changes in these views in the intervening time.

sentences.text: The CMC reported that officers perceived misconduct as less frequent and more likely to be detected, but were more willing to justify it.
sentences.support: However, there was a significant increase in the willingness of officers to justify occasions of misconduct.

sentences.text: The CMC identified continuing concerns about perceived favouritism, reporting misconduct and relationships with management.
sentences.support: including a perceived lack of protection from management for officers who report suspected misconduct

sentences.text: Its three recommendations covered recruitment and selection, compulsory ethics training and a review of internal misconduct reporting.
sentences.support: That Queensland Corrective Services systematically provide all staff, including management, with integrity and ethical training

findings.quote: However, there was a significant increase in the willingness of officers to justify occasions of misconduct.
CCOs seem reluctant to report misconduct and have generally unfavourable perceptions of senior staff and management.

notes: Survey findings describe officers’ perceptions, not proven incidents of misconduct.
